title: Design a Socratic plan review in docs/design/socratic-review.md
summary: Write one design document (no code) specifying a plan review between reading and dispatch: fixed question kinds, a cheapest-source-first answer ladder (facts, then Jev, then at most two user questions), recording, defaults-loop feedback, and failure attribution. It is grounded in the cited failures, with alternatives, per-job cost and the reader token budget.

defaults_applied.how: The deliverable is a written design with alternatives, to be reviewed before any build.
Each failure and number cites its source; unmeasured numbers are labeled estimates.
Written for an outside reader with terms defined.
The design includes a root-cause-versus-symptom question kind and failure-origin attribution.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The cited ids (D87, 9gwv, 16zf, nem8, 8qkc, m1bs, PR #59) are in records/ or docs/decisions.md, and the producer can read them from docs and BRIEF.md; where a record is unavailable the doc cites what is available and says so.
Jev is the rubric/gate component named in A6-4 and BRIEF.md; the design treats it as an existing typed-question interface and does not specify its internals.
Numbers for cost per job and reader budget are taken from athena.toml and records, or labeled as estimates.
Design only: no Rust, no config change, no new defaults.toml entries.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/socratic-review.md exists, contains no code changes elsewhere, and states the six fixed question kinds: assumptions, evidence the verifier can observe, file boundaries, decomposition, scope versus deliverables consistency, root cause versus symptom.

It defines the answer ladder: facts from code, records or the host first; then Jev as a typed question with a probability; then only the residue to the user, ranked by likelihood of changing the plan times cost of being wrong, capped at two questions.

It maps each failure to the question that would have caught it: D87, 9gwv, 16zf, nem8, 8qkc, m1bs, the four reader-budget retries, and the PR #59 'real repo' claim, citing the record or file each came from.

It specifies recording every question and answer, repeated identical answers becoming defaults-loop proposals, and weight increases when introspection traces a failure to an unasked or wrongly answered question.
It classifies each failure's origin as plan, execution, verification or environment, and defines honest acceptance (a bare 'athena go' without a prompt is not user acceptance).

It links to the BRIEF.md addendum 2026-10-14 and the 2026-10-13 addendum, A1, A2-4, A3 and A6-4, and includes an alternatives section, a cost-per-job estimate labeled as estimate or measured with its source, and the reader's token budget.
Run cargo test and cargo fmt --check; both still pass, since only docs changed (git diff --stat shows only docs/ and optionally CHANGELOG.md).

out_of_scope: Any Rust code, tests, or xtask changes
Implementing Jev or the defaults-loop changes
Reviewing the design (a separate review file under docs/design/reviews/)
departures: Cost and time are raised from the reference because the document is long, cites many records, and must reconcile several addenda; verification passing is lowered because content criteria are numerous and citations may be unverifiable.
